resumen: Legal vocabulary as used in the press and in administration: types of rules, courts, criminal and civil proceedings, and fundamental rights. Useful for commenting on court news and the regulatory framework.

explicacion.texto: The Anglo-Saxon system (common law) does not match the Spanish one, so many equivalents are approximate. Distinguish clearly between “law” (the law in general or a law), “act / statute” (a law passed by parliament) and “regulation” (Spanish “reglamento”).

filas: law / the rule of law
the system of rules, or one rule / the principle that everyone is subject to the law (es: derecho, ley / Estado de derecho)
The rule of law must be respected.
act / statute
a law passed by parliament (es: ley)
The Data Protection Act came into force in 2018.
to enact / to repeal
to make a law official / to cancel a law (es: promulgar / derogar)
The law was repealed in 2015.
to come into force
to start to apply legally (es: entrar en vigor)
The new rules come into force on 1 January.
to comply with / compliance
to obey a rule / the fact of obeying rules (es: cumplir / cumplimiento normativo)
Firms must comply with the regulation.
to breach / a breach of
to break a rule or agreement / a failure to respect it (es: incumplir, infringir / infracción de)
This is a breach of contract.
court / Supreme Court
a place where legal cases are decided / the highest court (es: tribunal / Tribunal Supremo)
The case went to the Supreme Court.
judge / jury
the person who runs a trial / the group of citizens who decide guilt (es: juez / jurado)
The jury found him guilty.
lawyer / solicitor / barrister
lawyer in general / lawyer who advises clients and does not usually argue in higher courts / lawyer who argues cases in court (UK) (es: abogado)
She hired a lawyer.
prosecutor / the prosecution
the lawyer who accuses someone on behalf of the state / the side that accuses (es: fiscal / la acusación)
The prosecution called three witnesses.
the defendant / the plaintiff (claimant)
the person accused or sued / the person who brings a civil case (es: el acusado, demandado / el demandante)
The defendant pleaded not guilty.
witness / evidence
a person who saw something / information that proves something (es: testigo / pruebas)
There was not enough evidence.
to sue (for)
to take legal action against someone (for something) (es: demandar (por))
She sued the company for damages.
to charge with
to formally accuse someone of a crime (es: acusar formalmente de, imputar)
He was charged with fraud.
trial / to stand trial
a legal process in court / to be tried in court (es: juicio / ser juzgado)
He will stand trial next year.
verdict / sentence
the decision on guilt / the punishment given (es: veredicto / condena, pena)
He received a five-year sentence.
to convict / to acquit
to find guilty / to find not guilty (es: condenar / absolver)
She was acquitted of all charges.
to appeal (against)
to ask a higher court to change a decision (es: recurrir)
They will appeal against the ruling.
ruling / judgment
an official decision of a court (es: fallo, sentencia)
The ruling sets a precedent.
bail
money paid so that an accused person can stay free until the trial (es: fianza, libertad bajo fianza)
He was released on bail.
fine
money paid as a punishment (es: multa)
The company was fined 2 million euros.
human rights / civil liberties
basic rights of every person / freedoms protected by law (es: derechos humanos / libertades civiles)
The law protects civil liberties.

items: “Sentence” is the punishment imposed; the court's decision is “ruling” or “judgment”.
“Jurisprudence” usually means legal theory; the body of court decisions (Spanish “jurisprudencia”) is “case law”.
“Process” is not a court case (Spanish “proceso judicial”): say “proceedings” or “trial”.

ejemplos.frase: The new law will come into force next spring.
ejemplos.traduccion: La nueva ley entrará en vigor la próxima primavera.

ejemplos.frase: He was charged with tax evasion and released on bail.
ejemplos.traduccion: Fue imputado por evasión fiscal y quedó en libertad bajo fianza.

ejemplos.frase: The jury acquitted her after three days of deliberation.
ejemplos.traduccion: El jurado la absolvió tras tres días de deliberación.

ejemplos.frase: The airline was sued by hundreds of passengers.
ejemplos.traduccion: Cientos de pasajeros demandaron a la aerolínea.

ejemplos.frase: The government will appeal against the court's ruling.
ejemplos.traduccion: El Gobierno recurrirá el fallo del tribunal.

ejemplos.frase: Landlords who fail to comply with the rules face heavy fines.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los caseros que incumplan las normas se enfrentan a fuertes multas.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The judicial process lasted three years.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The legal proceedings lasted three years.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A court case (Spanish “proceso judicial”) is “proceedings” or “trial”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The court's sentence says the law is unconstitutional.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The court's ruling says the law is unconstitutional.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Sentence” is only the punishment; the decision is “ruling” or “judgment”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She denounced her employer for unfair dismissal.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: She sued her employer for unfair dismissal.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “denunciar / demandar” in civil law is “sue”; “denounce” means to condemn publicly.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The law entered in vigour in May.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The law came into force in May.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “entrar en vigor” is “come into force” or “take effect”.

ejercicios.frase: The new regulation will come into ___ in January.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in the card includes to come into force (es: entrar en vigor), a fixed collocation in legal language. The clue is come into… followed by a date. An equivalent alternative would be take effect, but with come into only force is correct.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Come into force” = start to apply legally (es: entrar en vigor).
ejercicios.traduccion: El nuevo reglamento entrará en vigor en enero.

por_opcion.force: Correct: come into force = start to apply legally.
por_opcion.vigour: Incorrect: a calque of Spanish “vigor”; vigour in English means physical or mental energy.
por_opcion.effect of: Incorrect: you say take effect or come into effect, but never effect of in this position.
por_opcion.power: Incorrect: come into power means to take power (a government), not to come into force.

glosario.definicion_l: prescribed by or according to regulation · an authoritative command

ejercicios.frase: The Supreme Court's sentence declared the tax illegal.
respuestas: The Supreme Court's ruling declared the tax illegal.
The Supreme Court's judgment declared the tax illegal.
The Supreme Court's judgement declared the tax illegal.
The Supreme Court's decision declared the tax illegal.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card warns that sentence is only the punishment imposed (five years in prison); the court's decision is ruling or judgment. The clue is that the subject declares a tax illegal: it is a legal decision, not a punishment. Ruling, judgment, the British spelling judgement and the more general decision are accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: La sentencia del Tribunal Supremo declaró ilegal el impuesto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The Supreme Court's sentence declared the tax illegal.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: sentence is the punishment, not the decision.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The Supreme Court's verdict declared the tax illegal.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Verdict is the decision of guilty or not guilty, usually by the jury; for a court interpreting the law, ruling is used.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The Supreme Court's resolution declared the tax illegal.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Resolution is used for decisions of a political body (a UN resolution); a court's decision is ruling or judgment.

glosario.definicion_l: exercising power or authority · the reason for a court's judgment (as opposed to the decision itself)
an opinion formed by judging something · the act of judging or assessing a person or situation or event
a string of words satisfying the grammatical rules of a language · (criminal law) a final judgment of guilty in a criminal case and the punishment that is imposed

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a verb (es: demandar), in the past.
ejercicios.frase: The family ___ the hospital for negligence.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives to sue (for) (es: demandar (por)). It is a regular verb, and the instruction asks for the past: sued. The clue is for negligence, which gives the reason for the legal action, and the direct object the hospital, with no preposition.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Sue (for)” = take legal action against someone (for something).
ejercicios.traduccion: La familia demandó al hospital por negligencia.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Denounce means to condemn publicly; to take someone to a civil court is sue.
The instruction asks for the past: sued.
Demand means to ask for something firmly; to take legal action is sue.

glosario.definicion_l: failure to act with the prudence that a reasonable person would exercise under the same circumstances · the trait of neglecting responsibilities and lacking concern

ejercicios.frase: The former mayor was ___ with corruption.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives to charge with = formally accuse of a crime. The clue is the preposition with: only charge forms the collocation be charged with. Accuse also exists, but it goes with of (accused of corruption) and does not imply a formal charge.
ejercicios.traduccion: El exalcalde fue imputado por corrupción.

por_opcion.charged: Correct: be charged with = be formally accused of.
por_opcion.accused: Incorrect here: accuse goes with of, not with with (was accused of corruption).
por_opcion.blamed: Incorrect: blame means to say someone is responsible for something bad (blamed for), not to charge formally.
por_opcion.sued: Incorrect: sue means to take civil legal action and does not go with with.

ejercicios.frase: After a two-week trial, the jury ___ him of murder.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives to acquit (of) = find not guilty in a trial, the opposite of convict. The clue is the preposition of and the context: a jury at the end of a trial. Absolve is a false friend (Spanish “absolver”) used mainly in a religious or moral sense.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Acquit (of)” = find not guilty in a trial.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tras un juicio de dos semanas, el jurado lo absolvió del asesinato.

por_opcion.acquitted: Correct: acquit of = find someone not guilty of a crime in a trial.
por_opcion.absolved: Incorrect: absolve is used for forgiving sins or freeing someone from moral responsibility, not for a jury's verdict.
por_opcion.freed: Incorrect: free means to set free, but it does not form the structure free someone of murder.
por_opcion.released: Incorrect: release means to physically set someone free, not to declare them not guilty.

glosario.definicion_l: the act of testing something · trying something to find out about it
a body of citizens sworn to give a true verdict according to the evidence presented in a court of law · a committee appointed to judge a competition

ejercicios.frase: The suspect was released on ___ pending trial.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes bail (es: fianza, libertad bajo fianza) and the collocation released on bail. The clue is released on…, followed by pending trial (waiting for trial). Bail is uncountable and takes no article. In American English people also say released on bond, so bond is accepted, although the general and British form is bail.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Released on bail” = free after paying money until the trial (in the US also “on bond”).
ejercicios.traduccion: El sospechoso quedó en libertad bajo fianza a la espera de juicio.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “garantía”: being free until trial after paying is released on bail.
Bail is uncountable in this expression: on bail, with no article.

glosario.definicion_l: (criminal law) money that must be forfeited by the bondsman if an accused person fails to appear in court for trial
not as expected · someone who is under suspicion

ejercicios.frase: Companies must comply the new data protection rules.
respuestas: Companies must comply with the new data protection rules.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives to comply with = obey (a rule). Comply is intransitive and always takes with before what is obeyed. The mistake comes from Spanish “cumplir la norma”, with no preposition.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las empresas deben cumplir las nuevas normas de protección de datos.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Companies must comply the new data protection rules.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: with is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Companies must comply to the new data protection rules.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition after comply is with, not to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Companies must accomplish the new data protection rules.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Accomplish means to achieve or carry out; to obey a rule is comply with.

ejercicios.frase: Parliament voted to ___ the old law and replace it with a new one.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives to repeal = cancel a law, as opposed to to enact = make a law official. The clue is replace it with a new one: one law is removed to put another in its place. The card distinguishes repeal from appeal (ask a higher court to change a decision), two verbs that are confused because of their form.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Repeal” = cancel a law; “appeal” = challenge a court decision.
ejercicios.traduccion: El Parlamento votó derogar la antigua ley y sustituirla por otra nueva.

por_opcion.appeal: Incorrect: appeal means to challenge a court decision, not something Parliament does with a law.
por_opcion.repel: Incorrect: repel means to drive back, to resist an attack.
por_opcion.reveal: Incorrect: reveal means to make known.

glosario.definicion_l: a legislative assembly in certain countries · a card game in which you play your sevens and other cards in sequence in the same suit as the sevens; you win if you are the first to use all your cards

ejercicios.frase: The defence lawyer said they would ___ against the verdict.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives to appeal (against) = ask a higher court to change a decision. The clue is against the verdict: you appeal against a court decision. In British English you say appeal against; in American English, appeal the verdict, with no preposition.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Appeal against” = challenge a court decision (es: recurrir).
ejercicios.traduccion: El abogado defensor dijo que recurrirían el veredicto.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Repeal means to cancel a law; to challenge a decision is appeal.
Recur is a false friend of Spanish “recurrir”: it means to happen again.

glosario.definicion_l: (law) the findings of a jury on issues of fact submitted to it for decision; can be used in formulating a judgment

ejercicios.frase: He received a three-year prison ___ for fraud.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card states that sentence is the punishment imposed. The collocation a three-year prison sentence is the normal way to express a prison term. The clue is prison and the length of time, which only fit the punishment, not the decision.
ejercicios.traduccion: Le impusieron una condena de tres años de cárcel por fraude.

por_opcion.sentence: Correct: a prison sentence = a period in prison as punishment.
por_opcion.ruling: Incorrect: ruling is the court's decision, not the punishment; prison ruling is not idiomatic.
por_opcion.condemn: Incorrect: condemn is a verb (to criticise morally), not a noun.
por_opcion.verdict: Incorrect: verdict is the decision of guilty or not guilty, not the length of the punishment.

glosario.definicion_l: intentional deception resulting in injury to another person · a person who makes deceitful pretenses

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (es: multa); verb in the passive.
ejercicios.frase: The company was ___ 5 million euros for polluting the river.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes fine (es: multa), and the card reminds you that it is also a verb: to make someone pay a fine. The instruction asks for the passive, and the clue is was ___ followed by an amount. The regular past participle of fine is fined.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Fine” is also a verb: to make someone pay a fine.
ejercicios.traduccion: La empresa fue multada con 5 millones de euros por contaminar el río.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After was you need the past participle: fined.
Penalise means to punish in general, but the collocation with an amount of money is be fined + amount.

ejercicios.frase: The judicial process against the minister lasted four years.
respuestas: The legal proceedings against the minister lasted four years.
The trial of the minister lasted four years.
The proceedings against the minister lasted four years.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card warns that process is not a court case: in English you say (legal) proceedings or trial. The clue is against the minister, typical of proceedings against. Legal proceedings, proceedings and trial of are accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: El proceso judicial contra el ministro duró cuatro años.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The judicial process against the minister lasted four years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: process is a false friend in this sense.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The legal process against the minister lasted four years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is still the calque of Spanish “proceso”; the idiomatic form is legal proceedings.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The legal proceeding against the minister lasted four years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Proceedings, in this sense, is always plural.

glosario.definicion_l: (law) the institution of a sequence of steps by which legal judgments are invoked · a written account of what transpired at a meeting
a person authorized to conduct religious worship · a person appointed to a high office in the government

ejercicios.frase: Without the ___ of law, investors will not trust the country.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes the rule of law (es: el Estado de derecho), the principle that everyone, including the state, is subject to the law. The clue is the fixed structure the ___ of law. State of law is a calque that is not used in English.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “The rule of law” = Spanish “el Estado de derecho”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Sin Estado de derecho, los inversores no confiarán en el país.

por_opcion.rule: Correct: the rule of law = the principle that everyone is subject to the law.
por_opcion.state: Incorrect: a calque of Spanish “Estado de derecho”; state of law is not idiomatic.
por_opcion.reign: Incorrect: reign is the period a monarch rules; it does not form this expression.
por_opcion.government: Incorrect: government of law is not an established expression.

glosario.definicion_l: someone who commits capital in order to gain financial returns

ejercicios.frase: A key ___ refused to testify in court.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives witness (es: testigo). The clue is to testify (give evidence as a witness), which only a person can do: a key witness. Witness is countable and takes a.
ejercicios.traduccion: Un testigo clave se negó a declarar ante el tribunal.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Testimony is what is said in court; the person is witness.
The English word is required: witness.

glosario.definicion_l: someone who sees an event and reports what happened · a close observer; someone who looks at something (such as an exhibition of some kind)

ejercicios.explicacion: Plead (not) guilty = say formally in court that you are (not) guilty. The subject is the defendant (the accused), and not goes between the verb and guilty: pleaded not guilty. It is a fixed collocation in criminal proceedings; the table includes the exact example.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Plead (not) guilty” = say formally that you are (not) guilty.
ejercicios.traduccion: El acusado se declaró no culpable.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Not goes before guilty, not before the verb: pleaded not guilty.
Not comes before guilty.

glosario.definicion_l: a person or institution against whom an action is brought in a court of law; the person being sued or accused

descripcion_larga_es: Legal vocabulary as used in the press and in administration: rules (act, regulation), courts and legal professionals, criminal and civil proceedings (charge, trial, verdict, sentence, appeal) and fundamental rights. It is key for commenting on court news and the regulatory framework, and it is full of false friends for Spanish speakers: sentence is not Spanish “sentencia”, process is not a court case and denounce does not mean reporting someone to the police.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary of law and justice: how rules are passed, come into force and are repealed; who takes part in a trial (judge, jury, prosecutor, defendant, witness); and the stages of a case (charge, trial, verdict, sentence, appeal).
contexto.por_que_importa: Court and regulatory news appears constantly in the international press and in any economic policy topic (compliance, sanctions, fines). A false friend such as sentence for a ruling or process for court proceedings can change the meaning of what you report. In a C1 exam, precision in these collocations is expected.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When reading or summarising court news, explaining a legal reform, or talking about business regulation or fundamental rights. The signals are verbs such as charge, sue, acquit, comply, repeal and their fixed prepositions. Spanish speakers tend to translate “entrar en vigor”, “sentencia” or “denunciar” word for word.
